label: Tour Route
lede: The eleven stops and sixteen places on my free walking tour through the historic centre, one at a time. What you are looking at, why it is there, and the part most people walk past without seeing.
shelfLegendSub: Grouped by what each stop is really about

lead.title: Berlin War Damage Still Visible: The Walls That Were Never Repaired
lead.excerpt: Berlin never patched most of what April 1945 did to its walls. The clearest place to start is a free, open courtyard on Museum Island, where bullet strikes sit in the colonnade stone at the height of a standing person. Here are seventeen places across the city where the marks are still there to find, how to tell what made each one, and which two need planning before you go.
lead.alt: The rear of the ruined portico of the Anhalter Bahnhof in Berlin-Kreuzberg, its brick arches open to the sky with modern office towers behind
lead.line: Berlin never patched most of what April 1945 did to its walls.
